title: Pathology viva: adrenal incidentaloma and phaeochromocytoma

header.contentArea: Endocrine surgery: adrenal incidentaloma and phaeochromocytoma

related.why: Primary hyperparathyroidism, the other endocrine surgery viva and part of MEN 2
Anatomy of the kidney and its relations, including the adrenal glands

brief.scenario: Mr David Stanforth, 55, had a CT for suspected renal colic. It showed a 3.2 cm left adrenal mass. He takes amlodipine for hypertension.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on the investigation of this adrenal mass and, if it proves to be a phaeochromocytoma, its management.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Two questions for every incidentaloma: is it malignant, and is it secreting? Imaging answers one, hormones the other.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Deciding by size alone, or reaching for a beta-blocker before alpha-blockade.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "I want to know the unenhanced CT attenuation and whether it is producing hormones."

grid.label: Frame the problem
grid.fail: Plans surgery or discharge without stating what must be excluded.
grid.pass: Adrenal mass found on imaging for another reason; must exclude malignancy (adrenocortical carcinoma, metastasis) and hormone excess.
grid.high: Adds that most are benign non-functioning adenomas, and asks about prior cancer, since metastasis becomes more likely.

grid.label: Imaging
grid.fail: Operates or reassures on size alone, or biopsies first.
grid.pass: Unenhanced CT: homogeneous and 10 HU or less is a benign adenoma, whatever the size; no further imaging.
grid.high: Indeterminate lesion: further imaging (washout CT, MRI or FDG-PET) and MDT; biopsy rarely, never before phaeochromocytoma is excluded.

grid.label: Hormone tests
grid.fail: Omits tests, or tests only cortisol.
grid.pass: 1 mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test in all; aldosterone:renin ratio if hypertensive or hypokalaemic; plasma or urine metanephrines.
grid.high: States cortisol 50 nmol/L or less excludes autonomous secretion; metanephrines unnecessary if unenhanced attenuation is 10 HU or less.

grid.label: Recognise phaeochromocytoma
grid.fail: Cannot give its features or test.
grid.pass: Episodic headache, sweating and palpitations with hypertension; confirmed by plasma free or urinary fractionated metanephrines.
grid.high: Offers genetic testing, since many are hereditary (MEN 2, VHL, SDH variants); asks about family history.

grid.label: Preparation for surgery (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Starts a beta-blocker first or alone.
grid.pass: Alpha-blockade first (phenoxybenzamine or doxazosin) for 7 to 14 days; beta-blocker only afterwards for tachycardia.
grid.high: Explains unopposed alpha-stimulation causes a hypertensive crisis; adds high-sodium diet and fluids; involves an experienced anaesthetist.

grid.label: Surgery and aftercare
grid.fail: Plans open surgery by a non-specialist, with no postoperative monitoring.
grid.pass: Laparoscopic adrenalectomy by an experienced adrenal surgeon.
grid.high: Watches for hypotension and hypoglycaemia after tumour removal; lifelong follow-up with metanephrines.

pass.text: Whether it's malignant and whether it's secreting hormones.

pass.text: How do you assess malignancy risk?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Unenhanced CT attenuation. Homogeneous and 10 HU or less is a benign adenoma whatever its size.

pass.text: Overnight dexamethasone suppression test, aldosterone:renin ratio as he's hypertensive, and metanephrines.

pass.text: Attenuation is 32 HU. Plasma normetanephrine is raised. He describes episodes of headache and sweating.

pass.text: That's a phaeochromocytoma. The metanephrines confirm it.

pass.text: Alpha-blockade first, phenoxybenzamine or doxazosin, for 7 to 14 days, then a beta-blocker only if he's tachycardic.

pass.text: Laparoscopic adrenalectomy by an experienced adrenal surgeon.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Malignancy and hormone excess. Most are benign non-functioning adenomas, but I'd ask about previous cancer, because metastasis becomes more likely.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: It's 32 HU on the unenhanced scan.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: That's indeterminate. I'd discuss further imaging, washout CT, MRI or FDG-PET, at the MDT. I wouldn't biopsy, and never before excluding phaeochromocytoma.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Talk me through the hormone tests.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: A 1 mg dexamethasone test; cortisol 50 nmol/L or less excludes autonomous secretion. Aldosterone:renin ratio because he's hypertensive. At 32 HU he needs metanephrines; under 10 HU he wouldn't.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: That's phaeochromocytoma. I'd take a family history and offer genetic testing, because many are hereditary: MEN 2, VHL, SDH variants.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Why not start with a beta-blocker?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: It removes beta-2 vasodilatation and leaves alpha-constriction unopposed: a hypertensive crisis. Alpha first, with a high-sodium diet and fluids, and an experienced anaesthetist.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Watch for hypotension and hypoglycaemia once the tumour is out, and lifelong follow-up with metanephrines.

failures.consequence: Unopposed alpha-stimulation can cause a hypertensive crisis, stroke or death.

failures.move: Deciding on size alone, or biopsying first.
failures.consequence: A malignant mass is missed or a phaeochromocytoma is punctured, triggering a catecholamine crisis.
A secreting tumour is missed and he goes to theatre unprepared.
Relatives at risk and other tumours (such as medullary thyroid cancer in MEN 2) go undetected.

recovery.line: Unenhanced attenuation and hormone results decide it; size alone does not.
Alpha-blockade must come first; beta-blockade only after, for tachycardia.

knowledge.fact: Homogeneous mass of 10 HU or less on unenhanced CT: benign adenoma, no further imaging, whatever the size.
All incidentalomas: 1 mg dexamethasone test (cortisol 50 nmol/L or less is normal). Aldosterone:renin ratio if hypertensive or hypokalaemic. Metanephrines unless 10 HU or less.
Phaeochromocytoma: plasma free or urinary fractionated metanephrines; offer genetic testing.
Alpha-blockade for 7 to 14 days, high-sodium diet and fluids; beta-blockade only after alpha.

recall.think: Hypertensive crisis from beta-blockade first or biopsy of a phaeochromocytoma.
recall.say: "Is it malignant, and is it secreting?"
do: Alpha then beta, then laparoscopic adrenalectomy

numbers.meaning: Unenhanced attenuation at or below which a homogeneous mass is benign

recall.trap: Size alone does not decide; a small mass can still secrete.
recall.finish: Laparoscopic adrenalectomy after alpha-blockade; genetic testing; lifelong follow-up.

partner.opening: This man has a 3.2 cm left adrenal mass found on a CT for suspected renal colic. What worries you about it?

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks for the unenhanced attenuation
reveals.finding: 32 HU, slightly heterogeneous. No other abnormality.
Cortisol after 1 mg dexamethasone 38 nmol/L. Aldosterone:renin ratio normal. Plasma normetanephrine more than three times the upper limit of normal.
Episodes of pounding headache, sweating and palpitations over the past year. BP 168/102 in clinic.
His sister had a thyroid operation for 'cancer' in her thirties.

push.question: So a 5 cm mass automatically needs surgery?
push.expect: No: attenuation and hormones decide; a homogeneous mass of 10 HU or less is benign whatever the size.

push.question: Which hormone tests for every incidentaloma?
push.expect: Dexamethasone suppression test; aldosterone:renin if hypertensive or hypokalaemic; metanephrines unless 10 HU or less.

push.question: How do you prepare him for theatre?
push.expect: Alpha-blockade 7 to 14 days, then beta if tachycardic; salt and fluids.

push.question: What will you watch for after the tumour is removed?

curveballs.prompt: His heart rate is 120. Why not start a beta-blocker now?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Not before alpha-blockade: risk of hypertensive crisis. Beta only once alpha-blocked.
Decline until phaeochromocytoma is excluded; biopsy rarely changes management here.

curveballs.prompt: His sister had thyroid cancer young. Relevance?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Possible MEN 2 (medullary thyroid cancer): genetic testing and family screening.
